title: Data Residency Enforcement — Customer Pilot Tracker (Hosted + Dedicated)
content:
Purpose
- Single place to track enterprise/customer pilots for Hosted Data Residency Enforcement (region pinning + runtime enforcement + audit evidence).
- Used by CS/TAM + Product (Security & Compliance) to drive beta → GA readiness.

Definitions (quick)
- pinned_region: single region the org/project must run in (no cross-region fallback unless explicit exception).
- allowed_regions: list for multi-region allowed traffic (still enforced; outside list denied).
- Key success criteria (GA-ready for a pilot):
  1) Enforcement works at admission (deny before model execution) with correct error code and remediation link.
  2) No cross-region fallback when pinned (or exception workflow + audit event).
  3) Audit events present + exportable; customer can ingest into SIEM (Splunk/Sentinel).
  4) Console + SDK guidance is sufficient to prevent repeated violations.

Top recurring issues (rollup)
1) Wrong base URL / region endpoint used after enabling pinning
- Symptom: RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH spikes after enablement.
- Fix: update SDK config + enforce correct endpoint in CI/CD; add runbook step “check base URL + region hint.”

2) Confusion: pinned_region vs allowed_regions
- Symptom: customers set allowed_regions expecting auto-fallback; request “automatic” best region.
- Fix: docs + console copy: “no automatic cross-region fallback unless explicitly allowed + audited.”

3) Evidence packaging gaps
- Symptom: customers want sample payloads + retention + SIEM fields spelled out.
- Fix: provide short “audit evidence bundle” (sample events, exporter config, screenshots instructions).

4) Downstream write enforcement (analytics/persistence)
- Symptom: customers ask “do logs/traces/optional persistence stay in-region?”
- Fix: validate downstream pipelines per region; run dedicated E2E test with optional persistence toggled.

GA readiness checklist (CS-owned)
- [ ] At least 3 EU-pinned accounts complete a 7-day clean run (0 unexpected violations).
- [ ] At least 2 customers successfully ingest audit events into SIEM with Redwood-provided mapping.
- [ ] One Dedicated customer signs off on no cross-region fallback behavior + documented exception option.
- [ ] Console UX: customers can see effective policy + recent violations summary (even if limited).
- [ ] Support playbook updated (triage, what logs to ask for, escalation path).

Open questions / notes to self
- Need a standard “pilot enablement email” template w/ exact endpoint(s) and SDK snippets for each region.
- Should we formally recommend disabling client-side region hints when pinned? (seems like a footgun).
- For Private/VPC: align messaging so customers don’t assume Hosted guarantees apply 1:1.
